clue.text: Provider of children's entertainment, TV on leave

indicators.note: one thing tacked on to another is added after it, so the TV piece comes second, behind the leave piece

blocks.note: to jack in is British slang for to quit or leave a job
the box is informal for the television

explanation.surface: Somebody who entertains children is complaining that the television is off duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV on leave' reads as a broadcaster on holiday; in fact the TV piece sits on (after) the leave piece. To jack in is British slang for giving something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy whose clown springs out of a box, a classic amusement for small children.

clue.text: Psychologist married German woman in the Bernese Alps

definitions.note: a locating phrase standing for the mountain found there

blocks.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychologist
Frau is the German title for a married woman

explanation.surface: A psychologist marries a German woman and they settle in the Swiss mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in the Bernese Alps' points to a peak there, with the clue implying 'a mountain'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is one of the best-known peaks of the Bernese Oberland range in Switzerland.

clue.text: Dogs may be spooked reckons special

indicators.note: letters that are spooked are startled and scattered out of their order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone judges that some dogs are easily frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocker spaniels are a breed of small gun dog, so the plural fits the plural noun.

clue.text: At home, spinner for Middlesex initially playing his best

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a spinning top is a toy
taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A spin bowler for Middlesex, a county cricket side, is performing at his peak in a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a slow bowler in cricket, but here it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in top form means performing at one's peak, which is how someone playing his best would be described.

clue.text: Newspaper job?

blocks.note: the Financial Times, with its article, run together as one word

explanation.surface: A question about a position advertised in, or working on, a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper's name, The FT, run together makes the answer; 'job' is slang for a crime such as a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a job is a robbery or heist, so a theft is exactly such a job.

clue.text: Undemanding jockey in film

blocks.note: something undemanding is easy
a jockey rides horses

explanation.surface: A film features a jockey with an easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 American road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Have, in an excited state, to confess

blocks.note: to have something is to own it
being up means being lively or worked up

explanation.surface: Someone worked up into a state has to admit to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom for admitting guilt, the same as to confess.

clue.text: Beginning to realise Doctor No is no obscure novel?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so keep only that
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
the remaining letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone starts to realise that the Bond film Doctor No is hardly an unknown story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor No' looks like the Bond title, but Doctor is the instruction and No starts the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel of a castaway, so it is the very opposite of an obscure novel.

clue.text: Girl, extremely drunk, dropping CD

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the named letters are taken out

blocks.note: canned is slang for very drunk
the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: A girl so drunk she drops a compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking C and D out of CANNED leaves ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a common female first name, the usual crossword use of 'girl'.

clue.text: Ascot's winning margin? Short row follows

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the last letter goes
follows says this piece comes after the one before it in the answer

blocks.note: a horse can win by a neck
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A question about the margin of a win at Ascot racecourse, and a row behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the famous racecourse, which steers you to horse racing; but an ascot is also a broad necktie. 'Follows' puts the shortened row after the margin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide cravat-like piece of neckwear, a kind of tie.

clue.text: Mummy's boy, reportedly depressed when the day is done

definitions.note: a phrase for a time, standing for the noun

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: a mother's boy is her son
feeling down means feeling low

explanation.surface: A mother's son feels low as evening comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy's boy' looks like a clingy son, but it is just a son, sounding like the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is the time of sunset, the end of the day.

clue.text: Jumper next to mine in shabby cinema

blocks.note: a flea is a jumping insect
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A sweater lies beside a mine inside a run-down cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a British word for a sweater, which is the false path; here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleapit is British slang for a dingy, run-down cinema or theatre.

clue.text: Theatrical company to improve further performance

blocks.note: rep is short for a repertory company
to rise is to go up or improve

explanation.surface: A theatre company aims to get better with a repeat show.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeat performance of a piece or role, so it is a further performance.

clue.text: Escaped in cab, sodden, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A soaked fugitive got away in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to flee secretly, so escaped is the past tense synonym.

clue.text: Ground in lane with odd weed

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

blocks.note: part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange weed is growing on the ground in a lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil the weed grows in, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered plant usually treated as a weed in lawns.

clue.text: Project involving small fair

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to project is to stick out, or jut
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A plan involving a minor fête.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' and 'fair' both pose as nouns; one is the verb to stick out, the other means even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair are synonyms for impartial, treating people rightly.

clue.text: Astronaut, first from Georgia, hugged by Beatle on leaving

indicators.note: first from asks for the opening letter of the word that follows
leaving means departing, so the named letters go out
something hugged is held inside the arms of another

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
John Lennon of the Beatles
the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: An astronaut from Georgia gets a hug from a Beatle who is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatle is given in full, first and surname, and 'on leaving' trims the end of the surname before the G goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth, in 1962, and later a US senator.

clue.text: Hit man in SAS twice, unwisely

indicators.note: unwisely means foolishly done, so the letters are set down in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
SAS written two times

explanation.surface: A contract killer in the SAS, the British special forces, twice acted rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is a hired killer, which is what an assassin is.

clue.text: Homestead a long way away? Miles

blocks.note: something far is a long way off
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Is a homestead distant? Yes, miles away.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a farmhouse with its land, the same as a farm.

clue.text: Former PM leading workers in county

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this piece comes first in the answer

blocks.note: Lord North was British prime minister 1770 to 1782
worker ants

explanation.surface: A former prime minister heads a workforce in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' simply places the prime minister first.
explanation.definitionFit: Northants is the standard short form of Northamptonshire, an English Midlands county.

clue.text: Body of troops ordered to carry equipment

indicators.note: to carry is to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
a rig is a set of gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Soldiers have been told to bring their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as military command in the surface; it is the old past tense of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions, a body of troops.

clue.text: Polish fan

blocks.note: first meaning: to shine a surface
second meaning: an enthusiast

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To buff is to rub to a shine, and a buff is a keen enthusiast, as in a film buff.

clue.text: I depart after American friend

indicators.note: after places the departing phrase behind the abbreviation for the nationality

blocks.note: AM is an abbreviation for American
taken as written
to depart is to go

explanation.surface: Someone leaves following their friend from the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish for friend, widely used informally in English.

clue.text: Surprisingly large one, a country in Africa

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that one African country is surprisingly big.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is the largest nation in Africa by area, a fitting touch for the surface.

clue.text: Classically elegant upper room

blocks.note: first meaning: in the refined style of ancient Athens
second meaning: a room in the roof space

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a stylish top-floor room, but the two phrases are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes the pure style of Athens and Attica, and an attic is the space under the roof.

clue.text: Film director down in Italy

blocks.note: a fell is a hill or moor, like the downs
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A film director is feeling low while in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' suggests sadness, but it is upland: fells and downs are both open hills in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian director of La Dolce Vita and 8½.

clue.text: Locks in fortress, essential

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Locks on a castle are vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door fastenings in a fortress; they are lengths of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of hair, so both nouns are plural synonyms.

clue.text: Working with responsibility in a successful business

blocks.note: a machine that is going is working
a concern is a matter one is responsible for

explanation.surface: Someone works responsibly in a thriving company.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a business that is operating and profitable, the idiom for a thriving enterprise.
